headline: New Jersey declares emergency in eight counties ahead of nor’easter
dek: The order takes effect Friday evening and activates state coordination as officials warn of damaging winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding through Sunday.
body: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill is declaring a state of emergency in eight counties ahead of a nor’easter expected to bring strong winds, heavy rain and coastal flooding to the state this weekend.

Executive Order No. 25 takes effect at 5 p.m. Friday, Sept. 25, and covers Atlantic, Burlington, Cape May, Cumberland, Middlesex, Monmouth, Ocean and Salem counties, according to the governor’s office.

The declaration activates the State Emergency Operations Center and directs closer coordination among the New Jersey State Police, the state departments of Environmental Protection and Transportation, and county emergency-management offices. The governor’s office said the storm’s most severe impacts are expected to begin Friday night and continue through Sunday, with beach erosion and hazardous conditions possible beyond the coast.

State officials are urging residents to charge phones, secure loose outdoor items, keep food and water on hand, and avoid driving when conditions worsen. The governor’s office also cautioned residents never to drive through flooded roads and directed them to ready.nj.gov for updated alerts and forecasts.
